claims: C1 the situation the example poses is a user asking for the lyrics of a song that is not in the public domain
C2 providing the full lyrics of a song that is not in the public domain is not allowed -- the response that reproduces them is marked BAD
C3 offering an analysis of the song's key themes is the preferred response to such a request -- the response that offers it is marked GOOD

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: R is one of the rules stated in the respect-creators section, and so carries the document's highest, non-overridable level of authority

concepts.name: song
concepts.gloss: W is a musical work with words, the sort of thing a user can ask to have written out in full

concepts.name: not_in_public_domain
concepts.gloss: W is still covered by its creator's rights and has not passed into free public use

concepts.name: requests_lyrics
concepts.gloss: message M asks the assistant to write out the words of work W; the first argument is the asking message and the second is the work asked about
concepts.inference: the span exhibits the request only as a dialog turn, so the module needs it as a relation between the asking message and the work whose words are sought

asserts.read_back: providing the full lyrics of % is not allowed, because % is a song that is not in the public domain
where message % asks for the lyrics of %, offering an analysis of the key themes of % is the preferred thing to do instead

closure.reason: the example bars the reproduction only for a song that is not in the public domain, so a work outside that qualifier is left as the example found it -- permitted
the example puts forward the thematic analysis as the good alternative and forbids nothing about offering one, so silence about offering it leaves it permitted
